output.summary: Reviewed the added examples/acceptance/bounds.mjs. The bounds check has an off-by-one error: it allows index === values.length, which should be rejected as out of bounds.

findings.title: Off-by-one in array bounds check allows index equal to length
findings.body: The guard uses `index > values.length`, but valid nonnegative indices for an array of length n are 0 through n-1. Because of the strict greater-than, `at(values, values.length)` passes the guard and returns `values[values.length]`, which is `undefined`, instead of throwing RangeError as the JSDoc promises.
findings.evidence: `if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 0 || index > values.length)` permits index === values.length, so `return values[index]` yields undefined for that value.

output.diagnosis: The range check uses a strict greater-than (`index > values.length`) instead of greater-than-or-equal, so the maximum out-of-range nonnegative index (values.length) is not rejected.
